# Refuted claims and their evidence


- ❌ **[CRITICAL] The stated ΔG magnitudes are at or beyond the empirical ceiling for non-covalent binding: 6 of 25 exceed biotin–streptavidin, presented as routine output for 28–47-residue de novo peptides — Taken at face value (which is what the dashboard tile at index.html:74-75 and the leaderboard ΔG column at app.js:885 invite the reader to do), the stated free energies correspond to: -18.2 → 46 fM, -18.4 → 33 fM, -18.7 → 20 fM, -18.9 → 14 fM, -19.1 → 10 fM, -19.5 → 5.1 fM. Biotin–streptavidin, the canonical tightest non-covalent biological interaction, has Kd ≈ 4e-14 M → ΔG° = -18.28 kcal/mol (experimental value widely quoted as ≈ -18.3 kcal/mol). Six of the 25 candidates are therefore claimed to bind more tightly than biotin–streptavidin, and the flagship BasalSuper-AChE-TrkA-B5 (app.js:290) at -19.5 kcal/mol is claimed to be ~8-fold tighter than biotin–streptavidin. The remaining 19 sit between -15.2 and -17.8, i.e. 7 pM to 90 fM — still tighter than essentially any reported de novo designed peptide. For calibration, the best affinity-matured de novo mini-protein binders from state-of-the-art structure-based design reach roughly 20 pM to 10 nM (Cao et al., Nature 2022), i.e. ΔG° of -14.6 to -10.9 kcal/mol; unoptimized first-round designs are typically µM–nM. There is no ligand-efficiency argument that rescues these: -19.5 kcal/mol over the ~295 heavy atoms of a 39-mer is LE ≈ 0.066 kcal/mol per heavy atom, which is not itself anomalous, but the total is, because the interface a 28–47-residue linear peptide can bury is small and largely unpreorganized (these are flexible chains, several with unpaired cysteines and GGGGS linkers, so a large conformational-entropy penalty applies before any interface term is counted). The claimed affinities are also asserted uniformly across six unrelated target classes (RTK ectodomains, an AChE gorge, a Kelch β-propeller, a Frizzled CRD, a pentameric LGIC ECD, a membrane transporter), which is itself implausible — achievable affinity is strongly target- and epitope-dependent. Consequence: Femtomolar affinity is effectively irreversible on any biological timescale; a compound with Kd = 5 fM would not dissociate from its target over the lifetime of the cell, which contradicts the platform's own claim of 'Tolerance Downregulation < 4.2%' and reversible allosteric tuning (README.md:100-102). It also makes the safety narrative incoherent: at 5 fM the drug would be quantitatively bound to every copy of the target at concentrations far below one molecule per cell (one molecule in a 1 pL cell is ~1.7 nM). Any reviewer, grant panel, or partner with binding-thermodynamics training will read the -18 to -19.5 kcal/mol column as an immediate red flag and discount the entire repository, including the parts that are sound.**
